Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:1045-1053)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.AnyPlayer in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

OnUse (protected override, SneckoOil.cs:.issue: Rollup of guards N2 and N3 per binding rule 4. The structure is right and it is the part a replay would notice: draw 7 FIRST, then walk the resulting hand in order and take ONE `Rng.CombatEnergyCosts.NextInt(4)` per non-X card (SneckoOil.cs:47-56 vs potions.py:1048-1053). What diverges is the second filter clause the port drops (N2) and the until-played half of SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed (N3), both dormant.

guards.what: N1: the draw comes first, so the seven new cards ARE randomised; and the draw count on the stream matches
guards.rationale: SneckoOil.cs:47 draws before :48 reads the hand, so the potion randomises the cards it just drew as well as the ones already held; potions.py:1048-1050 does the same. One CombatEnergyCosts NextInt(4) per eligible card, in hand order, on both sides -- the sim reads `ctx.combat.combat_rng.energy` (potions.py:1049) and calls `randrange(4)` per card. A wrong count or a wrong stream here would be grade A, so it is verdicted rather than folded into OnUse.

guards.what: N2 (dormant): the C# skips a card whose unmodified cost is NEGATIVE and the port has no such clause
guards.issue: SneckoOil.cs:51 guards each card with `if (item.EnergyCost.GetWithModifiers(CostModifiers.None) >= 0)` on top of the `!c.EnergyCost.CostsX` filter at :48. potions.py:1051-1053 ports only the CostsX half. DORMANT because the sim has no representation for a negative cost at all: Card.energy_cost clamps with `max(0, ...)` (cards/base.py:232) and the stored `_energy_cost` is set from the card's own class attribute, so no ported card can present a negative unmodified cost for the guard to catch. What would make it live: giving the sim an unclamped cost representation (the game uses negative values as sentinels), at which point the sim would randomise a card the game skips AND take an extra CombatEnergyCosts draw doing it -- which is a stream desync, so this dormant entry is worth more than its grade suggests.

guards.what: N3 (dormant): `SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed` also expires when the card is PLAYED; the sim models only the end-of-turn half
guards.issue: SneckoOil.cs:53 calls `EnergyCost.SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed(...)`, whose name states two expiry conditions. The sim's counterpart is Card.set_cost_this_turn (cards/base.py:252-258) and its own docstring concedes the difference: 'The game's modifier also expires when the card is played; the sim only tracks the end-of-turn half, which differs solely for a card played and returned to hand in the same turn.' Verdicted against the CODE and the claim holds -- `_cost_this_turn` is cleared only by reset_turn_cost_modifiers (cards/base.py:265-268), called at turn start (player.py:154-155), and nothing in the play path clears it. DORMANT: the divergence needs a card that is played and returns to the hand in the same turn while carrying a randomised cost, and no such route is exercised today. What would make it live: porting any effect that returns a played card to hand within the turn (the game's Rebound-shaped cards). Not this record's mechanism to fix -- cards/base.py is shared, and relic/snecko_eye is the other consumer -- but no existing record verdicts it, so it is filed here rather than dropped.

guards.what: N4: `TestEnergyCostOverride` is a TestMode branch and the port takes the shipping arm
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 18 checked explicitly: SneckoOil.cs:59-66's NextEnergyCost returns `TestEnergyCostOverride` when it is >= 0 and the Rng draw otherwise, and the setter is guarded by `TestMode.AssertOn()` (:37) so the field can only be set from test code. The default is -1 (:19), so the shipping game always takes `Rng.CombatEnergyCosts.NextInt(4)` -- which is the arm potions.py:1053 ports. This is the trap that caught relic/calling_bell, and this unit does not fall into it.
